result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse explicitly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing, and callers (e.g. Office365CalendarService, ZoomVideoAdapter, SalesforceCalendarService) persist `tokenResponse.data` / the parsed key directly into prisma.credential. So a literal sentinel string can be stored as the refresh token, and a later non-shared refreshOAuthTokens path would send this bogus value to the provider, breaking token refresh. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff and is a real correctness defect introduced by this change.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse mutates refreshTokenResponse.data to inject a sentinel refresh_token of the literal string "refresh_token", which is then persisted to the database by callers (Office365, Google, Salesforce, Zoom). A credential whose provider omits refresh_token (expected under credential sharing) gets the literal string 'refresh_token' stored as its refresh token; any code path that later falls back to non-shared mode and calls refreshOAuthTokens with this stored value will send a bogus refresh token to the provider, and the sentinel is indistinguishable from a real token so tests cannot detect the corruption without asserting exact DB content.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function explicitly mutates the parsed result to inject a literal sentinel when the provider response omits `refresh_token`: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. Callers then persist refreshed credentials back to Prisma (e.g., Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates `prisma.credential`), which would overwrite a real refresh token with the literal string when running in the “credential sharing” mode where refresh_token may be omitted. If credential sharing is later disabled (env-based `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`), refresh flows that use the stored refresh token would send the bogus literal to providers. This is a correctness/data-corruption issue introduced by the diff.
